_about: Budgets are ratios against a yardstick measured in the same run (zlib over fixed bytes, never this project's code), because seconds recorded on one machine cannot gate another. One entry per operating system: the ratio travels only part of the way -- a Linux runner read 0.56x of the laptop's budget -- so each platform carries what was measured on it. The seconds are for a reader, not what is compared.

Linux._from: read out of CI run 35358714204, one measurement per interpreter, and averaged. The three agreed within 20% on the corpus and 58% on the PDF layer, so the mean sits where no healthy interpreter warns; recording the lowest would have left 3.12's ordinary PDF pass reading 1.58x.

Windows._from: read out of CI run 35358714204. One measurement, not three: this is the only interpreter the gate runs there. A single sample is thin, which the generous thresholds absorb -- and a second sample will arrive with the next push, as a factor rather than as a new budget.
